subject: Question: data sovereignty and transient cross-region processing for Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme-analytics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-analytics.com, Anna Lee <anna.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency / routing question for pilot

Hi Priya / Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — excited to move our inference pilot forward. Before we sign the SOW we need a couple of clarifications from the platform/security side:

1) Can Redwood commit that customer inference data for our account (Acme Analytics) will be pinned to the US region (AWS us-west-2) for both request processing and logs?
2) Do you ever do transient cross-region processing (e.g., fallbacks, cache population, or disaster recovery) that would cause data to leave the pinned region? If so, what controls and retention limits apply?
3) We need a copy of your current subprocessor list and SOC2 evidence.

Our concern: some of our datasets have regulated PII and our legal team requires clear limits on cross-border processing except for brief failover windows.

Can you share the exact language you would include in the DPA about region pinning and the maximum window for transient replication or caching? Also please attach the subprocessor CSV and SOC2 summary.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Analytics
samir.gupta@acme-analytics.com
[Attachment: pilot_requirements.xlsx]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natanajan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency / routing question for pilot

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:
- We can offer account-level region pinning for request processing and for persistent logs/artifacts (yes, can be pinned to us-west-2).
- We do allow ephemeral cross-region processing in limited cases (DR failover, cache warm-up, very short TTL replication) but we can set contractual caps and notification requirements.
- I'll attach the DPA draft and the subprocessor export; SOC2 summary attached as well.

A couple of quick clarifying questions to make the DPA language specific:
- Which of the payload classes do you consider regulated? (PII, special categories, raw audio, etc.)
- What is your acceptable maximum window for any transient replication or caching? (examples we use: 5 minutes, 1 hour, 24 hours)
- Do you require audit log retention in-region only, or is aggregated metadata acceptable outside the region?

If you can respond to the above, we can produce a DPA amendment with explicit maxima and a DocuSign-ready copy for signature.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, subprocessors_2025-10.csv, SOC2-type2-summary.pdf

—Priya
Priya Natarajan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_nathanajan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency / routing question for pilot

Hi Samir — adding technical context on the transient behaviours Priya mentioned. I own runtime routing here.

How our runtime behaves:
- Primary: All inference requests for a pinned account are routed to the customer-configured region (us-west-2). KV caches and model activations are provisioned in-region.
- Ephemeral cross-region activity: In the event of a regional outage or capacity shortage we have two mechanisms that may cause short-lived processing outside the pinned region:
  * Cache warm-up: to maintain latency, we may pre-warm a warm-standby in an adjacent region for up to 10 minutes before routing back; data in the warm-standby is held encrypted and scrubbed of request payloads after the warm period.
  * DR failover: we can failover to a designated recovery region; per our proposed contract language this would be invoked only after automated 3-minute detection + manual 15 minute confirmation and is limited to a 2-hour window unless extended by mutual agreement.

Logging and metadata:
- Full request/response payloads are retained only in the pinned region by default.
- Aggregated telemetry (metrics, aggregated latency histograms) may be replicated out of region for product analytics; we can exclude request identifiers or PII from those aggregates by default for your account.

Proposed DPA snippets (draft language you can use):
"Data residency: Redwood will process and store Customer Data in the US region (us-west-2) except as explicitly permitted below. Transient cross-region processing is allowed only for (i) cache warm-up for up to 10 minutes, and (ii) disaster recovery failover for up to 2 hours unless Customer provides written approval to extend. All transient processing will use encryption-in-transit and at-rest and will be logged; access to transient copies will be restricted to personnel with explicit emergency access and will be scrubbed of non-essential payload fields upon termination of the transient window."

I attached the current subprocessor export (subprocessors_2025-10.csv) and a short SOC2 summary. Happy to tighten the numbers if your legal requires 5 minutes instead of 10 for warm-up — we can propose that as well.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme-analytics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_nathanajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, security@acme-analytics.com, Anna Lee <anna.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Oct 2025 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency / routing question for pilot

Thanks — that helps a lot. Our security team reviewed the draft language and we propose the following adjustments before signing:
- Limit cache warm-up to 5 minutes (rather than 10).
- Require automated notification to our security mailbox and an audit entry whenever transient cross-region processing is invoked.
- Retain an in-region-only copy of full request logs for 90 days; aggregated telemetry may be replicated out of region without identifiers.

If you can update the DPA with those three items we can route to procurement and execute via DocuSign. Please include the DocuSign link for the finalized DPA and confirm the HubSpot deal record to tie this to the SOW.

Next steps: Priya/Marcus — can you send an updated DPA with the 5-minute warm-up cap and notification clause? Once we have that we'll start a legal review and should be able to sign within 72 hours.

Best,
Samir
